image_targets.codex: colony cassette recorder in a dry wall niche above a flooded pump bay floor, racked-out breaker cabinet open behind it, paper lockout tag still wired to the handle
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: close view of a lockout tag, initialled, hanging on a breaker that is clearly withdrawn

en_US.title: Pump Bay 12 Log, Maintenance Shift 4
en_US.scanner: Colony cassette recorder, niche mount, tape readable, four entries. Confidence 84 percent. Hazard: bay discharge header pressurised. Limit: cannot confirm the drive bus is dead.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Pump Six primes with its breaker racked out, and this tape is the only record of how often.

Four entries across nine days, each with the lockout tag hung and initialled. A contactor jarred closed by hand vibration accounts for the first two. The last two were logged with the bay bus isolated at both ends, and the recording keeps that contradiction rather than settling it.

Crews started knocking on the discharge casing to make it prime. Two hand injuries that month sit under the same work order number.

Assessment: the header can come up to pressure at 2,215 metres while every panel in the bay reads dead. Crack the test port before you trust a tag, including your own.
en_US.terminal: DOCUMENT 44-M-1188. ROOM: PUMP BAY 12. FINDING: INTERMITTENT PRIME, SOURCE UNIDENTIFIED. CLASS: PRESSURE VARIANCE, NON-REPORTABLE. INJURY ENTRIES: 2, EQUIPMENT CONTACT. TAG REVIEW: DEFERRED, PARTS.
en_US.field_note: Two crushed hands filed as equipment contact, which is accurate and tells you nothing about why the equipment moved. Crack the test port yourself. That tag is paper, not a switch.
en_US.audio: -- log, Shift Four, second entry, because the first did not take. Pump Six, Bay Twelve. Breaker is racked out, lockout tag is mine, I am looking at it. Two knuckles on the discharge casing and it primes. Nine seconds. Eleven, sorry, eleven. [suit fan, then a low mechanical surge] Day shift says a contactor jars closed. Bus is dead both ends, I megged it myself. Crew is queuing up to knock on it like it owes them something, and I want that on record before somebody puts an arm in the header. File it as pressure variance, that is the only box that clears. [surge resumes] That is it running with my tag on the --
en_US.external_site_article:
Recovery crews working Sector 44 have recorded intermittent priming of a discharge pump in a bay whose breaker was withdrawn and tagged. Four events are documented over nine days by the maintenance shift that held the lockout, two of them with the bay bus isolated at both ends.

No cause has been established. Deep Reach filed the entry as pressure variance and deferred the tag review pending parts, a classification that describes a reading without describing a pump. Two hand injuries recorded in the same bay that month carry the same work order number.
en_US.external_site: Recovery crews working Sector 44 have recorded intermittent priming of a discharge pump in a bay whose breaker was withdrawn and tagged. Four events are documented over nine days by the maintenance shift that held the lockout, two of them with the bay bus isolated at both ends.

image_targets.codex: handheld dictation unit clipped to a hanging gas ledger outside a dormitory hatch, wall atmosphere panel behind it showing a single needle at nominal
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: wall panel reading 101 kilopascals total pressure with no oxygen field on the face at all

en_US.title: Shift B Air Count, Dorm Nine
en_US.scanner: Handheld dictation unit clipped to a gas ledger. Confidence 76 percent. Hazard: room reads nominal total pressure. Limit: no partial-pressure history stored on the unit.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Dorm Nine held 101 kilopascals of total pressure while its oxygen fraction fell, and the wall panel called that nominal.

Total pressure is the sum of every gas in a room. Carbon dioxide off nineteen sleeping bodies replaced the oxygen close to one for one, so the sum held and the needle never moved. A Shift B clerk caught it on a pocket cell during a routine count, four hours before the morning relief would have cleared the room on the total.

The ledger for that period is countersigned twice. The second signature is not a name the roster carries.

Assessment: no habitat panel in Sector 44 reads partial pressure. Carry your own oxygen cell and read a room before you unseal, not after.
en_US.terminal: DOCUMENT 44-A-0442. ROOM: DORM 9. ATMOSPHERE: WITHIN TOTAL PRESSURE TOLERANCE. FLAG: OXYGEN FRACTION, OPERATOR REPORTED, INSTRUMENT UNVERIFIED. CLASS: CALIBRATION DRIFT. OCCUPANCY THAT PERIOD: NOT RECORDED.
en_US.field_note: Occupancy not recorded, because recording it would have made the oxygen number somebody's problem. Bring your own cell. That panel still reads nominal, forty-three years after the last person in there stopped breathing.
en_US.audio: Shift B air count, Dorm Nine, oh four twenty. Total is a hundred and one kilopascals, nominal, ledger balances, sign it and go to bed. Except my cell says oxygen partial seventeen point one. Sixteen point nine. It is falling while I talk. [breath, page turn] The sum holds because carbon dioxide is filling the hole, and the panel only sums, it does not read. Whoever has the six: do not clear Dorm Nine on total pressure. Not on total. Get a partial. There are nineteen -- there are people asleep in ther--
en_US.external_site_article:
A dormitory atmosphere record from Sector 44 documents a room holding 101 kilopascals of total pressure while its oxygen fraction dropped through 17 percent, the shortfall taken up by exhaled carbon dioxide. Habitat panels of that generation summed total pressure and displayed no partial-pressure field, so the wall reading stayed nominal throughout.

The discrepancy was found on a hand-carried oxygen cell during a shift count. Deep Reach recorded the operator report as calibration drift and left the panel in service. Occupancy for the period is not entered on the sheet.
en_US.external_site: A dormitory atmosphere record from Sector 44 documents a room holding 101 kilopascals of total pressure while its oxygen fraction dropped through 17 percent, the shortfall taken up by exhaled carbon dioxide.

image_targets.codex: hardwired watch-station recorder on a desk facing a large viewport, exterior floodlights visibly dimmed, no creature clearly visible in the water outside
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: lighting panel showing north bank at 20 percent output with no fault lamp lit

en_US.title: Observation Bay 4 Watch Log
en_US.scanner: Watch-station recorder, hardwired, tape spliced twice. Confidence 69 percent. Hazard: north floodlight bank on automatic gain. Limit: no exterior camera to correlate.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
The north floodlight bank at Observation Bay 4 throttles itself to twenty percent whenever a body holds station in the beam.

Those lamps run on a photocell that measures returned light and trims current to hold a set brightness. Something large and pale sitting sixteen metres out reflects enough of the cone back into the cell that the circuit reads the wall as overlit and pulls power. Nothing trips. Nothing logs. The bay goes dark while the panel shows full output, and the watch is left facing a window with no light behind it.

Two watch logs describe the shape as flatter than it is wide. Neither describes it leaving.

Assessment: put the north bank on manual current from the corridor panel before you approach that glass at 1,895 metres.
en_US.terminal: DOCUMENT 44-O-0907. ROOM: OBSERVATION BAY 4. FAULT: NORTH LIGHTING BANK, OUTPUT REDUCTION, INTERMITTENT. CLASS: CALIBRATION DRIFT, LIGHTING. VIEWPORT: RATED. WATCH POSTING: MAINTAINED, SINGLE OCCUPANT.
en_US.field_note: A lighting fault, they called it, and kept one person alone at the glass through every shift of it. Throw the bank to manual from the corridor, then walk in. Not while you are stood at the window.
en_US.audio: Window watch, Bay Four, hour six of eight, delighted. Floods on the north face went to twenty percent again. Not tripped. Throttled. The photocell reads the wall as lit and trims the current, and the wall is not lit, there is a body in the beam kicking light back into the sensor. Sixteen metres out. Call it eight. [chair, then a click as the lamps drop] So put the north bank on manual. On manual, from the corridor panel, before your watch, not during, because when it comes in close the lamps take themselves down and you are stood at a black window with-- [tap on glass]
en_US.external_site_article:
An observation-bay watch record from Sector 44 documents repeated output reduction on an exterior floodlight bank with no fault indication. The bank held automatic gain from a photocell measuring returned light, and reflection off a large body holding station in the beam was sufficient to drive output to roughly twenty percent.

The effect leaves the panel reading normal while the compartment loses illumination. Deep Reach classified the behaviour as lighting calibration drift, kept the viewport rated, and maintained a single-occupant watch posting on the bay.
en_US.external_site: An observation-bay watch record from Sector 44 documents repeated output reduction on an exterior floodlight bank with no fault indication.

image_targets.codex: belt recorder on the deck beside a pulled scrubber canister, grey fused absorbent spilled across the plates, plant panel behind showing green on every bed
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: open scrubber canister packed with sintered grey ash instead of loose granular media

en_US.title: Scrubber Three Bed Swap, Habitat Tech
en_US.scanner: Belt recorder, filter-plant issue, casing scorched. Confidence 81 percent. Hazard: spent absorbent, residual heat and caustic dust. Limit: bed weights not stored on the unit.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
A sintered scrubber bed runs warm and reads on the panel exactly like a working one.

Carbon dioxide absorption gives off heat, so the plant treats a warm bed as an active bed. Media regenerated past its cycle limit fuses into a grey ash that still holds temperature and holds no capacity at all. Beds Three and Five at the atmosphere plant were ash and green on the same morning, which cost the habitat something near forty hours of breathable margin that nobody had budgeted for.

Eleven regenerations above rating were signed off against a requisition number that returns nothing.

Assessment: weigh the canister. Dry mass at or under 4.1 kilos means spent, cycle count over forty means spent, and temperature means nothing whatsoever.
en_US.terminal: DOCUMENT 44-H-2310. PLANT: ATMOSPHERE, SCRUBBER 3. MEDIA: WITHIN THERMAL SPECIFICATION. CAPACITY TEST: NOT SCHEDULED. CLASS: MATERIAL RETENTION, CONSUMABLES. REGENERATION CYCLES APPROVED ABOVE RATING: 11.
en_US.field_note: Material retention, consumables, meaning they kept re-cooking the thing that keeps people breathing until it turned to ash. Weigh a bed before you believe the plant readout. The panel in there still shows green.
en_US.audio: Habitat tech, bed swap, Scrubber Three, and I want this on the tape. [canister thud, grit underfoot] Media is ash. Warm ash. It runs warm because it is sintered, not because it is pulling anything, and the panel reads warm and calls it green. Bed Three is ash. Five is ash. That is forty hours of breathing that is not in this building and nobody upstairs has -- [cough] -- weigh the canisters. Do not read the temperature, weigh them. Four point one kilos dry means done. I signed the last eleven regenerations because the requisition was -- because the requisition. Just weigh them.
en_US.external_site_article:
A filter-plant record from Sector 44 documents carbon dioxide absorbent regenerated repeatedly above its rated cycle count until the media fused. Fused beds retain the temperature rise that plant instrumentation uses to infer absorption, so an exhausted bed and a working bed present the same signature on the panel.

Two beds on one scrubber train were found spent while indicating normal, against an estimated forty hours of habitat breathing margin. Deep Reach recorded the practice as material retention against consumables, and no capacity test was scheduled on the train.
en_US.external_site: A filter-plant record from Sector 44 documents carbon dioxide absorbent regenerated repeatedly above its rated cycle count until the media fused. Fused beds retain the temperature rise that plant instrumentation uses to infer absorption, so an exhausted bed and a working bed present the same signature on the panel.

image_targets.codex: structures recorder magnet-clamped to a welded pressure rib in a long flooded corridor, chalk frame numbers stencilled along the steel, hammer resting against the web
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: close view of a continuous welded rib passing through a frame web, hammer-tap witness marks around it

en_US.title: Rib Survey, Frames 22 to 29
en_US.scanner: Structures recorder, magnetic clamp, still attached to the rib. Confidence 87 percent. Hazard: unverified coupling at Frame 26 web. Limit: bearing taken off a rib is meaningless.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Voices arrive in rooms that share no air, no door and no sightline, because the pressure ribs carry them there.

Steel conducts sound near 5,000 metres per second against roughly 1,500 in water. The frames are welded continuous through the factory, so a shout in Bay 22 lands in Bay 6 ahead of itself and arrives with no direction on it whatever. Crews called the effect the choir and used it to find casualties, which sent rescue parties into empty rooms.

Part way through this survey, Rib 6 began carrying the pump deck, which hangs off a separate run. The dye check on Frame 26 came back clean.

Assessment: one clamp on a rib gives you no bearing at 2,240 metres. Two clamps on separate frames and the arrival difference will.
en_US.terminal: DOCUMENT 44-S-0631. SURVEY: PRESSURE RIBS, FRAMES 22-29. FINDING: ACOUSTIC TRANSFER, UNPLANNED PATH. DYE CHECK FRAME 26: NEGATIVE. CLASS: PRESSURE VARIANCE, MONITOR. RESCUE PROCEDURE: UNCHANGED.
en_US.field_note: They wrote the transfer down, left the rescue procedure alone, and let the next crew keep running to the wrong room. Two clamps on two frames, time the difference, then move.
en_US.audio: Structures, rib survey, Frames Twenty-Two to Twenty-Nine, second pass. It is not a choir. Steel carries sound three times faster than water, the ribs are welded continuous, so a voice in Bay Twenty-Two arrives in Bay Six because both bays hang off the same rib. Fine. Here is what I do not like. Yesterday Rib Six carried the pump deck. The pump deck is not on that run. [hammer, long ring] And stop using the ribs to find people, you will go to the wrong room. I went to the wrong room on Tuesday and stood there holding the -- Dye check Frame Twenty-Four. Twenty-Six. Both, before shift chan--
en_US.external_site_article:
A structures survey from Sector 44 documents speech transmitted between compartments with no shared atmosphere or opening. Welded pressure ribs conduct sound at roughly three times its speed in water and deliver it without usable bearing, so a voice raised in one bay is audible in another and appears to originate locally.

Colony crews used the effect to locate casualties and were repeatedly sent to unoccupied compartments. The survey also records one rib run picking up a deck on a separate run, with a negative dye check at the suspect frame. Rescue procedure was left unchanged.
en_US.external_site: A structures survey from Sector 44 documents speech transmitted between compartments with no shared atmosphere or opening.

image_targets.codex: steward's recorder half buried in a spilled box of printed route cards at a muster gate, all cards showing the same corridor number, stanchion tape torn
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: single printed route card reading CORRIDOR 6 with a pencil number added beside it

en_US.title: Muster Two Queue Log
en_US.scanner: Steward's recorder in a card box, 900-count stock, most cards unissued. Confidence 92 percent. Hazard: printed route enters flooded corridor. Limit: no issue tally on the tape.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Every card in the Muster Two box sends its holder into Corridor 6, which took water at 02:00 while the cards were still being handed out.

The board line to the print shop was down and the plate was never struck. One steward stood at the head of the queue, read the correction into a recorder, and shouted it at each person in turn, which holds for exactly as long as a single voice holds against an alarm loop and a crowd that is already moving.

Roughly 900 cards are left in the box. Twelve of them carry a second corridor number in pencil, in a different hand.

Assessment: a card recovered here is printed proof of a route that is not there. Take the room numbers off the ink and route yourself.
en_US.terminal: DOCUMENT 44-E-6006. STATION: MUSTER 2. CARD STOCK: 900, CORRIDOR 6. CORRIDOR 6: FLOODED 2147, PRESSURE VARIANCE. PLATE CORRECTION: NOT ISSUED. QUEUE TALLY: BLANK. CLASS: DOCUMENT CONTROL, MINOR.
en_US.field_note: Document control, minor. Nine hundred cards aimed into a flooded corridor and the finding lands on the print shop. If you pick one up, trust the room numbers and nothing about the arrow.
en_US.audio: Muster Two, queue log, on tape because nobody picks up the board line. [crowd, alarm loop] The cards say Corridor Six. Corridor Six took water at oh two hundred. I have four hundred -- I have a box of nine hundred cards that all say Six and a line that does not stop. If you are holding a Six you go to the brine stair. Brine stair. Say it back. [voice off mic] Sir, I need you to -- whoever prints the next lot, strike Six off the plate. Off the plate, not off the -- [thud] -- I have got my own card here and it say--
en_US.external_site_article:
A muster-station record from Sector 44 documents printed evacuation route cards continuing to be issued after the routed corridor had flooded. The correction was passed by voice at the head of the queue because the station line to the print shop was out and the printing plate was never altered.

Roughly nine hundred cards remain in the box, all naming the same corridor. Deep Reach filed the matter under document control as a minor finding, with the station's issue tally left blank.
en_US.external_site: A muster-station record from Sector 44 documents printed evacuation route cards continuing to be issued after the routed corridor had flooded. The correction was passed by voice at the head of the queue because the station line to the print shop was out and the printing plate was never altered.

image_targets.codex: recorder on a ledge in a small service alcove, wall covered in chalked hand outlines and knuckle prints with valve numbers and crosses written over them, binder open on the floor
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: chalked valve number with two crosses beside it, hand outline underneath

en_US.title: Alcove Nine Work Order, Colony Maintenance
en_US.scanner: Recorder left on a ledge among hand-marks. Confidence 74 percent. Hazard: wall chalk indicates live cross-tie at Valve 4. Limit: markings undated.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
The chalk on the wall of Alcove Nine is a more accurate valve map than the binder on its floor.

The oldest marks are hand outlines pressed flat to the concrete, one to a crew. Later outlines carry a valve number written across the palm. The newest are scratched into the coating, by somebody in gloves with no time, and they use a notation the drawings never had: two crosses for cross-tied to a live header.

Valve 4 carries two crosses. The binder shows Valve 4 isolated. A work order to remove unauthorised surface marking was closed as complete with the wall untouched.

One outline lies under sprayed sealant applied before the alcove entered service.

Assessment: read the wall at 2,060 metres first, and treat any valve carrying two marks as live whatever the drawing says.
en_US.terminal: DOCUMENT 44-C-0919. ROOM: SERVICE ALCOVE 9. WORK ORDER 44-C-0919-B: UNAUTHORISED SURFACE MARKING, REMOVE. STATUS: CLOSED COMPLETE. VALVE 4: ISOLATED PER DRAWING. HOUSEKEEPING: DEFICIENT, RECURRING.
en_US.field_note: The drawing says Valve 4 is isolated and the wall says it will kill you. Only one of those was written by somebody standing in the room. Two marks means live, whatever the binder says.
en_US.audio: Colony Maintenance, Alcove Nine, work order reads remove unauthorised surface marking. [brush on concrete, then it stops] I am not scrubbing this wall. Half of it is hand outlines, which is what people do. The other half is a valve map, and it is right, and the drawing in the binder is not. Two crosses means cross-tied to the live header. Valve Four has two crosses. Binder has Four isolated. Somebody scratched that one in, not chalked. Gloves on, no time. And there is an outline at the skirting the size of my -- [breath] Order stands. Closing it complete. Wall stays. Read Nine before you turn anything in that ro--
en_US.external_site_article:
A maintenance record from Sector 44 documents an informal chalk valve map maintained by work crews in a service alcove, over an older layer of hand outlines and knuckle prints. Crew notation marked valves cross-tied to live headers, and disagrees with the plant drawing on at least one valve.

The removal order raised against the markings was closed as complete without the wall being cleaned. Deep Reach carried the alcove as a recurring housekeeping deficiency and left the drawing in force.
en_US.external_site: A maintenance record from Sector 44 documents an informal chalk valve map maintained by work crews in a service alcove, over an older layer of hand outlines and knuckle prints. Crew notation marked valves cross-tied to live headers, and disagrees with the plant drawing on at least one valve.

image_targets.codex: office dictation cylinder on a desk beside a period-close roster sheet with badge numbers struck through, bank of closed suit lockers visible through the doorway
image_targets.scanner_thumbnail: colony badge with a period-close stamp across the face, roster line struck through behind it

en_US.title: Payroll Period Close, Sector 44
en_US.scanner: Office dictation cylinder, administrative issue, spooled to the end. Confidence 65 percent. Hazard: none local. Limit: cannot recover the roster being read from.
en_US.in_game_wiki:
Atmosphere allocation in Sector 44 was calculated off the active payroll roll, so closing a badge stopped counting the body attached to it.

Scrubber sizing, bunk assignment and suit issue all keyed to one roster. A badge moved to asset reassignment left that roster while the worker stayed on shift: the plant stopped sizing air for them, the locker stopped issuing them a seal, and neither change was communicated to the worker. Thirty-four badges closed in a single period. None of the thirty-four appear on a departure manifest.

The form to reopen a badge took eleven days.

Assessment: the locker and door panels down here still test a badge against that roster. A recovered badge is a key only if it was open when the power went, so read the stamp before you carry it 95 metres for nothing.
en_US.terminal: DOCUMENT 44-P-1204. PERIOD CLOSE: SECTOR 44. BADGES CLOSED: 34, ASSET REASSIGNMENT. ATMOSPHERE PLAN: ADJUSTED TO ROLL. DEPARTURE MANIFEST ENTRIES: 0. CLASS: ADMINISTRATIVE, ROUTINE. REVIEW: NOT REQUIRED.
en_US.field_note: Thirty-four reassignments, zero departures, class routine, review not required. Read the stamp on any badge you lift: an open one still opens lockers, a closed one is a piece of tin with a dead man's number on it.
en_US.audio: Payroll, period close, Sector Forty-Four, and I want somebody above me to hear this. The atmosphere plan pulls off the active roll. Off the roll. So when a badge goes to asset reassignment, the plant stops counting that body, the locker stops issuing to it, and the body is still on shift, still breathing, still queuing at the -- [keys, drawer] Thirty-one closed this period. Thirty-four. Thirty-four, I have the sheet in front of me. None of them are on a departure manifest, where would they even -- if your badge reads closed you go to the Contract Continuity Desk before shift. Before. After is a form, and a form is eleven d--
en_US.external_site_article:
An administrative record from Sector 44 documents habitat atmosphere allocation, bunk assignment and suit issue all keyed to the active payroll roster. A badge closed under asset reassignment therefore removed a worker from air planning and equipment issue while that worker remained rostered on shift, with no notice to the individual.

Thirty-four badges were closed in one period against no departure manifest entries. Deep Reach recorded the period close as administrative and routine, with review not required, and the reinstatement form ran eleven days.
en_US.external_site: An administrative record from Sector 44 documents habitat atmosphere allocation, bunk assignment and suit issue all keyed to the active payroll roster.
